questions.question: At approximately what requests per second does LiteLLM start breaking down in production benchmarks?
questions.explanation: Kong's published benchmark shows LiteLLM experiencing cascading failures around ~2,000 RPS on an 8 GB memory footprint. The lesson recommends it for Python apps under 500 RPS and dev/staging gateways.

questions.question: Kong's own benchmark on the same 12-CPU hardware showed Kong AI Gateway was how much faster than LiteLLM?
questions.explanation: Kong's benchmark on 12 CPUs: Kong AI Gateway was 859% faster than LiteLLM and 228% faster than Portkey. This throughput advantage matters when you exceed ~500 RPS and need consistent low latency.

questions.question: Which AI gateway went Apache 2.0 open-source in March 2026 and is positioned on guardrails, PII redaction, and audit trails?
questions.explanation: Portkey went Apache 2.0 open-source in March 2026. It is control-plane-positioned with guardrails, PII redaction, jailbreak detection, and audit trails. Production tier costs $49/month and adds 20-40 ms per-request latency overhead.

questions.question: What drives the self-hosted versus managed gateway decision according to the lesson?
options: Cost — self-hosted is always cheaper at scale
Data residency — if requests must not leave your network, self-host
Latency — self-hosted adds less overhead than managed
Feature parity — managed gateways lack advanced routing
questions.explanation: Data residency is the primary driver for self-hosting a gateway. If regulatory or contractual requirements prevent sending request data through a third-party managed proxy, you must self-host. Portkey and Kong both offer OSS + optional managed to serve this spectrum.

questions.question: Which gateway is described as the best fit for regulated industries needing guardrails and observability bundled?
questions.explanation: Portkey bundles guardrails, PII redaction, jailbreak detection, and audit trails — making it the regulated-industry pick. Kong AI Gateway is the scale pick if you are already on Kong. LiteLLM is for dev/prototyping.

questions.question: Which gateway pattern does Bifrost (Maxim AI) implement as a canonical recipe?
options: Semantic caching of repeated LLM responses
Automatic retry with configurable backoff and fallback to Anthropic on OpenAI 429 errors
Request deduplication to prevent duplicate charges
Cost-based routing to the cheapest available model
questions.explanation: Bifrost implements automatic retries with configurable backoff and the canonical recipe of falling back to Anthropic when OpenAI returns a 429 (rate limit). This is the multi-provider failover pattern in its simplest form.
